title: Quantitative and Temporal Control of Oxygen Microenvironment at the Single Islet Level
protocol: Dissect C57BL/6 mice.
Isolate islets by collagenase digestion and Ficoll density gradient separation.
Incubate isolated islets in RPMI-1640 medium containing 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 20 mM HEPES.
Culture islets for 24 hours prior to use.
Use the islets within 1-2 days of isolation.
Generate microstructure geometries on transparency photomasks for each device layer.
Pour degassed, premixed PDMS to a height of 1.5 mm in a blank Petri dish and cure at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Punch 2 mm diameter input/out ports.
Spin two 350 μm layers of SU8-2150 on a 4 inch silicon wafer.
Expose UV light through the appropriate photomask to transfer microchannel pattern onto the SU8 after development.
Pour degassed, premixed PDMS onto this master to a height of 3 mm and cure at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Cut the cured PDMS to shape with a razor blade.
Punch 2 mm diameter input/output ports on the cured PDMS.
Spin SU8-2100 to 100 μm for membrane fabrication.
Apply UV-lithography to transfer microwell patterns onto the 100 μm tall master.
Spin degassed, premixed PDMS at 900 rpm for 30 seconds and cure at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
Repeat spinning of PDMS with the same conditions to achieve a 200 μm thickness.
Punch 2 mm diameter input/output ports through the membrane layer.
Spin SU8-2100 to 100 μm for gas microfluidic layer fabrication.
Apply UV-lithography to transfer gas microfluidic patterns onto the 100 μm tall master.
Pour degassed, premixed PDMS on top of the gas microfluidic layer to a height of 1.5 mm and cure at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Cut the PDMS to shape with a razor blade.
Punch 2 mm diameter input/output ports through this gas microfluidic layer.
Clean layers with scotch tape, expose them to corona arc.
Align the membrane layer by hand.
Bond the membrane layer to the bottom gas layer facing up.
Bond the glucose microfluidic layer on top of the microwell membrane.
Encapsulate the assembly by bonding the inlet and outlet layer on top.
Add 1 kg weight on top and bake at 100 °C for 3 hours to reinforce bonding.
Load water into the aqueous layer for leak testing.
Submerge the entire device under water during leak testing.
Flow air through the gas layer with an empty syringe.
Sterilize leak-free devices with 70% ethanol through the aqueous layer then flush with PBS buffer, in which the device is stored at 4°C until use.
Obtain 2 microdispensers, 5 V and 20 V DC power supplies, and a digital I/O board to construct the oxygen mixing and delivery setup.
Connect the microdispensers' control leads to the included driver units.
Connect the drivers to the digital I/O board at ports corresponding to Labview controls.
Connect the 5 V and 20 V power supplies to corresponding contacts on the drive units.
Connect the digital I/O to a laptop to execute Labview codes for gas control.
Connect one microdispenser to nitrogen while another to compressed air, both with 5% CO2.
Set both gases to 2 psi.
Hook up the dispensers' outputs in a T-junction prior to entering the microfluidic device.

Using a leak-tested device, characterize the transient response of oxygen modulation by cycling the microdispensers between 5-21% oxygen while measuring dissolved oxygen in water with a fiber optic oxygen sensor.
Mount the device to the heated stage on the inverted microscope.
Connect 0% and 21% O2 gases to the device and calibrate with the oxygen sensor.
Connect the output port of the glucose microfluidics to a fraction collector.
Prepare Krebs Ringer bicarbonate buffer with the specified composition.
Add 2 mM glucose to prepare a low-glucose KRB solution.
Add 14 mM glucose to prepare a high-glucose KRB solution.
Heat both buffer solutions to 37°C in water baths.
Connect peristaltic pump tubing and flow over a 37°C hotplate before entering the microfluidic device.
Stain islets by adding Fura-2 AM and Rh123 to KRB at final concentrations of 5 μM and 2.5 μM, respectively.
Incubate stained islets in dye solution for 30 min at 37°C.
Load approximately 20 islets into the device via the glucose microchannel inlet.
Prime buffer from the outlet back into the inlet to direct islets into the chamber.
Perfuse islets with buffer for 10 min to wash away excess dyes.
Deliver a glucose stimulation pulse of 5 min baseline followed by 15 min at 14 mM, then wash for 15 min in KRB2.
Record measurements at 340/380 nm excitation wavelength for Fura-2 and 534 emission for Rh123 during the glucose stimulation pulse.
Measure a normal pulse (14 mM normoxic) before each experiment to establish baseline.
During oxygen modulation experiments, apply buffer flow only during stimulation and washing steps.
Collect effluents from glucose outlet at 1 min intervals for ELISA insulin assay.
